title: Phrae 2 Days 1 Night 2026 — Old Town, Teak Houses & Wat Phra That Cho Hae | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A well-paced 2-day, 1-night Phrae itinerary in northern Thailand: Old Town, Khum Chao Luang, Ban Wongburi, the 130-teak-pillar Ban Pratapjai, and Wat Phra That Cho Hae — plus where to eat, where to stay, and real costs.
keywords: Phrae 2 days 1 night, Phrae itinerary, Phrae Old Town, Wat Phra That Cho Hae, Ban Pratapjai, Khum Chao Luang
h1:
Phrae in 2 Days, 1 Night
Old Town, Teak Houses & Cho Hae
intro: Phrae is a small, easy town to walk, with the highlights clustered around the Old Town and a few spots just outside it — which makes it a great fit for a weekend trip. This plan spends day one walking the Old Town and the antique teak houses, then wraps up at the walking street, while day two heads up to Wat Phra That Cho Hae and stops for indigo-dyed mor hom cloth before you leave. The timing is realistic with room to breathe — no rushing — and comes with food spots and a rough budget ready to go.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Phrae is that everything sits close together. Khum Chao Luang, Ban Wongburi, and the Old Town temples are nearly all within walking distance of one another, while Wat Phra That Cho Hae and Ban Thung Hong are on the edge of town, a drive of no more than 15–20 minutes. Two days and a night is plenty to see it all at an unhurried pace. A private car or a rented motorbike is the smoothest way to get around, since Phrae doesn't have much in the way of public transport within the town to rely on.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old Town, Teak Houses & the Walking Street

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: An easy walk around Phrae's Old Town

items.note: A teak mansion built in 1892 during the era of Chao Phiriyathepwong, in a gingerbread style that blends Thai and European touches — the fretwork along the eaves and the ventilation panels are gorgeous. It's now the Phrae City Museum, an easy 45 minutes or so of strolling and photos.

A pink teak house in a colonial-meets-Lanna style, over a hundred years old, dating back to the reign of King Rama V. Inside, the original furnishings and everyday items are still kept on display. It's a very short walk from Khum Chao Luang, with an entry fee of just a few tens of THB.

items.activity: Old Town temples — Wat Phong Sunan / Wat Phra Non
items.note: The temples inside the old city walls are close together, so you can visit them one after another on foot. The atmosphere is quiet and not crowded.

items.activity: Lunch — Phrae-style khanom jeen nam ngiao
items.note: Phrae's nam ngiao has a clear-broth recipe — rounded in flavor, not too intense — and you'll find it around town, for example near the back of Nareerat School by the Pratu Chai gate. Order it with crispy pork rind and fresh veg and you'll fill up for 40–60 THB.

A house built entirely of teak, using 130 large teak pillars, started in 1972. It's the spot everyone who comes to Phrae stops to photograph. Open 08:00–17:00, entry 20 THB for Thais and 40 THB for foreigners. It's on the edge of town, about a 10-minute drive from the Old Town.
A Burmese–Shan style wooden temple with a tiered roof and finely carved woodwork — an unusual piece of architecture compared with the typical Lanna temple.

items.activity: Coffee break in the Old Town
items.note: Phrae has several old wooden-house cafés in the Old Town, for example along Kham Lue Road. Rest your legs before heading to the walking street.

It runs on Saturday evenings, roughly 16:00–20:00, on Kham Lue Road near Ban Wongburi, with local food, handicrafts, and local performances. If your trip doesn't land on a Saturday, look for a northern-Thai restaurant in town instead.

blocks.title: Day 1 tip
blocks.html: Kad Kong Kao only runs on Saturday evenings. If you want to walk the night market, plan the trip so your first night falls on a Saturday — that's when you'll get the full atmosphere.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Wat Phra That Cho Hae & Mor Hom Cloth

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Pay respects at the temple, then shop for gifts before heading home

items.note: Grab khao ngiao, rice porridge, or old-style coffee in town before you set off — a light meal is enough to fuel the temple visit.

Phrae's guardian stupa, and the year-of-the-tiger birth-year stupa. The chedi is clad in gleaming gold jangko sheeting. Open daily 06:00–19:00, about 9 km from town, a 15–20 minute drive. Leave time to climb the naga staircase and pay your respects.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Phra That Doi Leng (if you have time)
items.note: It's up the hill past Cho Hae, with a wide view over Phrae — good for shots from up high. If you'd rather not keep driving the mountain road, you can skip it; it's optional.
Head back into town for a northern-Thai restaurant. Try kaeng hang le, nam phrik num with steamed veg, or khua yam to round out the meal.

items.activity: Ban Thung Hong — buy mor hom cloth
items.note: The mor hom village (cloth tie-dyed with indigo from the hom plant), about 4 km from town, with shops lined up along the road. Pick up genuine mor hom clothing as a gift — prices are reasonable, and it's Phrae's signature product.

items.activity: Souvenir shopping to close out the trip
items.note: Beyond mor hom cloth, Phrae's popular souvenirs include khao kaep (rice crackers), Chinese pastries, and local snacks. Pick some up before the drive home.
Leave Phrae in the late afternoon and you can drive or catch a bus back at an easy pace, no need to rush.

blocks.title: Driving up to Cho Hae & Doi Leng
blocks.html: The road up to Wat Phra That Cho Hae is flat and smooth, but if you carry on up to Doi Leng it gets steep and winding. If you're new to mountain driving, go in the morning while it's bright and check your brakes first.

Phrae has places to stay ranging from in-town hotels within walking distance of the Old Town to wooden-house resorts with a local feel. Staying in the town area suits this plan best, since you'll head out to the walking street in the evening and want an easy trip back to bed.

items.name: Hotels in the Old Town area
items.blurb: Walking distance to Khum Chao Luang, Ban Wongburi, and the walking street. Good if you don't have a car — easy to head out for an evening stroll.

items.name: Wooden-house resorts on the edge of town
items.blurb: Quiet and leafy, good if you have a car and want more privacy. The drive into town isn't far.

blocks.label: Top 10 Phrae Hotels →

items: 1 night's stay — in-town hotels start around 500–1,200 THB/room (cheaper split between two)
Food for 2 days — about 400–700 THB if you eat mostly at local spots
Entry fees — Ban Pratapjai, Khum Chao Luang, and Ban Wongburi add up to a low few hundred THB in total
Fuel / car rental — a motorbike runs about 200–300 THB/day, or fuel for your own car as needed
Souvenirs — mor hom cloth and snacks as you like; set aside around 300–500 THB

blocks.html: All in, a budget 2-day, 1-night Phrae trip comes to roughly 1,500–2,500 THB per person. Travel as a pair and split the room and transport, and it works out even better value.

blocks.text: Getting to Phrae and around town

items: Bus / minivan — buses run daily from Bangkok and Chiang Mai to the Phrae bus terminal
Flights — Phrae Airport has flights from Bangkok, but they're limited, so check the schedule in advance
Private car — the most convenient, with easy parking, since the sights are spread across both the town and the outskirts
Motorbike rental — rental shops in town make it nimble for running between the Old Town and Cho Hae

faq.q: Is 2 days and 1 night enough for Phrae?
faq.a: Comfortably, yes. Phrae's highlights are clustered in the Old Town and the nearby outskirts, so two days covers the Old Town, the antique teak houses, Wat Phra That Cho Hae, and buying mor hom cloth before you leave. If you want to add nature like Phae Mueang Phi or a waterfall, bump it up to 3 days and 2 nights.

faq.q: Which day should I visit Phrae to catch the walking street?
faq.a: Kad Kong Kao, the Phrae walking street, runs mainly on Saturday evenings. If you want to walk it, line up the first night of your trip with a Saturday for the fullest food and atmosphere.

faq.q: What are the opening hours for Ban Pratapjai and Wat Phra That Cho Hae?
faq.a: Ban Pratapjai (the Hundred-Pillar House) is open 08:00–17:00, entry 20 THB for Thais and 40 THB for foreigners. Wat Phra That Cho Hae is open daily 06:00–19:00 with no entry fee.

faq.q: Can I visit Phrae without my own car?
faq.a: You can, but it takes a bit of planning. You can walk to almost everything in the Old Town, while for Cho Hae and Ban Thung Hong on the outskirts, it's best to rent a motorbike or hire a local songthaew/taxi for those legs.

faq.q: What souvenirs should I buy in Phrae?
faq.a: Mor hom indigo cloth from Ban Thung Hong is the number-one signature buy, followed by khao kaep (rice crackers), Chinese pastries, and local snacks. You can find them both at Ban Thung Hong and at souvenir shops in town.
